rationale: M60 XML deep review, finding X6. A self-loop guard read `if (type === References || type === Imports) { if (source === target) return }`, on the reasoning that a thing cannot reference or import itself. Sound for a REFERENCE, where source and target are both component names and equality really is a cycle in the document. Unsound for an IMPORT, because the two ends are DIFFERENT KINDS OF THING: `source` is a symbol name and `target` is a path read out of a SYSTEM identifier. `<!ENTITY cover.gif SYSTEM "cover.gif" NDATA gif>` names a real file called cover.gif, and the guard discarded the edge. It discarded it ASYMMETRICALLY, which is what makes it a defect rather than a policy: `extractExternalId` had already pushed the ImportInfo a few lines earlier, so the file was present in the analyzer's `imports` array and absent from its relationship graph — the analyzer contradicting itself inside a single call, with the graph the part consumers read. 46 such edges in the corpus (libxslt's docbook and general suites are full of `<!NOTATION GIF SYSTEM "GIF">`). Nothing is lost by narrowing the guard: there is no meaningless self-import for it to prevent, since a file named after the declaration that names it is still a second thing. Lines read off the file: cover 3, cover.gif 4, jpeg 5, plain 6. The `plain` entity is the control: its name and path differ, so it was already emitted, and pinning it proves the fixture is not merely asserting the new behaviour. `cover` and `cover.gif` differ by a dot and nothing else, so a normaliser that stripped path punctuation would collapse them and quietly pass a broken analyzer.

forbidRelationships.note: each entity imports its OWN system id; cover.gif importing cover.jpg would be a file crossed between two declarations, and the two differ only by a dot
